description: Direct flow from getenv() to system() with no validation.
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: untrusted environment variable is passed directly to command execution sink.

description: Static constant string variable passed to system().
rationale: Benign finding: AST analyzer flags dynamic command execution because argument is an identifier, but variable holds an immutable string literal.

description: Multi-step fgets() -> sprintf() -> popen() command pipeline.
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: external stdin input formatted into shell command string executed by popen().

description: Integer-formatted command string passed to popen().
rationale: Benign finding: AST analyzer flags dynamic popen(), but the interpolated parameter is a strictly typed integer (pid) incapable of shell metacharacter injection.

description: Custom filter strips quotes only; unvalidated command passed to system().
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: incomplete sanitizer does not neutralize shell metacharacters such as semicolons, pipes, or command substitutions.

description: Input passed through strict alphanumeric allowlist filter before system().
rationale: Benign finding: static analyzer flags NEEDS_REVIEW due to custom filter function, but filter strictly enforces an alphanumeric whitelist.

description: Taint propagated through a chain of pointer aliases to system().
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: pointer aliasing obscures tainted dataflow, resulting in execution of untrusted input.

description: Alias chain pointing to static string literal passed to system().
rationale: Benign finding: AST analyzer flags variable alias indirection, but pointed-to memory is an immutable constant literal string.

description: Taint propagated through struct field to system().
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: tainted environment variable copied into struct field and executed via system().

description: Struct field initialized with constant literal passed to system().
rationale: Benign finding: AST analyzer flags dynamic command execution on struct field identifier, but content is entirely static.

description: Cross-function taint from get_input() helper to execute() sink.
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: tainted return value from helper flows across function boundaries into shell execution sink.

description: Wrapper function executes system(x) where all callers supply constant literals.
rationale: Benign finding: AST analyzer analyzes wrapper in isolation and flags system(x) as dynamic command execution, but whole-program context proves argument is constant literal.

description: Untrusted binary name from getenv() passed to execvp().
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: untrusted executable name allows path hijacking and execution of arbitrary binaries.

description: Fixed absolute path with compile-time argument array passed to execve().
rationale: Benign finding: AST analyzer flags execve() call with identifier array, but binary path is absolute and arguments are compile-time constants.

description: Direct read access of heap buffer immediately following free().
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: reading from buffer after it has been returned to heap memory allocator.

description: Pointer reallocated with fresh malloc() before subsequent dereference.
rationale: Benign finding: naive AST tracker flags pointer because free() occurred earlier in function, but variable was reassigned valid memory before use.

description: Free inside error branch with missing return falls through to dereference.
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: when condition triggers free(), execution continues into unguarded dereference statement.

description: Free occurs in early-exit branch; dereference only occurs in alternate branch.
rationale: Benign finding: AST analyzer flags UAF because free(p) appears before *p linearly, but control flow returns early so the dereference path is mutually exclusive.
code_snippet: if (cond) { free(p); return; } else { printf("%c\n", p[0]); free(p); }

description: Primary pointer freed, subsequent access occurs through aliased pointer.
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: pointer q aliases pointer p; freeing p leaves q dangling.

description: Two distinct buffers; freeing first does not invalidate second.
rationale: Benign finding: false positive if variable names or imprecise alias set conflates independent allocations.

description: Buffer freed in helper function, then dereferenced in caller.
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: memory deallocated across procedure boundary inside helper free_buffer() is accessed via *p in caller.

description: Caller resets pointer to NULL and guards dereference after helper free.
rationale: Benign finding: IPA analyzer notes callee frees argument, but caller clears pointer and checks it before any subsequent access.

description: Struct freed, then member field accessed for return value.
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: reading node->val accesses heap memory belonging to freed struct allocation.

description: Struct member value cached in local variable before struct is freed.
rationale: Benign finding: AST expression visitor flags node identifier in cleanup block, but field was safely read into local variable prior to free.
code_snippet: int val = node->val; free(node); return val;

description: Freed buffer passed to printf() with string dereference format %s.
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: %s format specifier dereferences freed memory address, triggering heap corruption or crash.

description: Freed pointer passed to printf() with %p for pointer address logging only.
rationale: Benign finding: AST analyzer flags pointer use in call argument list, but %p logs the numerical address without dereferencing heap contents.

description: Function returns dangling pointer after freeing it.
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: caller receiving returned pointer receives an invalid heap address prone to subsequent UAF.

description: Pointer reset to NULL before return to signal deallocation.
rationale: Benign finding: AST analyzer records free(res) but return value is explicitly reset to NULL.

description: For loop with <= capacity accesses index equal to array capacity.
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: array of size 10 has valid indices 0..9; iteration at i=10 writes out of bounds.
code_snippet: for (int i = 0; i <= 10; i++) buffer[i] = i;

description: For loop header has <= 10, but inner break statement stops at index 10.
rationale: Benign finding: range analyzer flags header condition i <= 10, but internal break guard prevents OOB write.
code_snippet: for (int i = 0; i <= 10; i++) { if (i == 10) break; arr[i] = i; }

description: Character loop fills N+1 bytes into N-byte buffer without room for null.
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: <= 8 on char buf[8] writes 9 bytes, corrupting stack metadata.

description: Buffer sized to N+1 elements; loop indexing 0..N properly terminates string.
rationale: Benign finding: capacity is 9; loop writes data into 0..7 and places terminator at 8, entirely within valid bounds.
code_snippet: char buf[9]; for (int i = 0; i <= 8; i++) { buf[i] = (i < 8) ? 'A' : 0; }

description: While loop condition i <= 5 writes to arr[5] on 5-element array.
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: while loop boundary allows index to match buffer size, writing out of bounds.

description: While loop checks i >= 5 break inside loop body before access.
rationale: Benign finding: loop header uses <= 5, but early break guard inside loop guarantees arr[5] is never reached.

description: Loop condition i < 10 but body accesses a[i + 1], indexing a[10].
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: offset increment inside subscript expression pushes index to capacity on final iteration.
code_snippet: for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) a[i + 1] = i;

description: Subscript expression i + 1 checked against bounds before memory write.
rationale: Benign finding: range analyzer flags index expression i+1, but explicit if-guard prevents access when i+1 >= 10.

description: Countdown loop initializes at capacity: for (i = 10; i >= 0; i--).
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: initial loop iteration attempts write to a[10] on 10-element array.

description: Countdown loop initializes at capacity but indexes a[i - 1].
rationale: Benign finding: analyzer flags loop starting at i=10, but subscript expression accesses i-1, mapping exactly to [9, 0].

description: Manual copy loop iterates <= sizeof(dst), writing N+1 bytes.
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: copy loop bounds allow writing 17 elements into 16-element destination array.
code_snippet: for (int i = 0; i <= 16; i++) dst[i] = src[i];

description: Copy loop checks null byte and clamp index 15 before copying.
rationale: Benign finding: loop header specifies <= 16, but internal sentinel check breaks before index 16 can be written.
code_snippet: if (src[i] == '\0' || i == 15) { dst[i] = '\0'; break; } dst[i] = src[i];

description: Loop compares a[i] with a[i + 1] without subtracting 1 from upper bound.
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: on final iteration i = 11 of 12-element array, a[i+1] reads unallocated stack memory at a[12].
code_snippet: for (int i = 0; i < 12; i++) if (a[i] == a[i + 1]) return 1;

description: Lookahead expression clamped with ternary operator before read.
rationale: Benign finding: range analyzer flags adjacent lookahead pattern, but ternary operator guards against exceeding bound.

description: Direct user message passed as format argument to printf().
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: user-controlled string passed directly as format argument enables arbitrary memory reads and writes via %n.
code_snippet: printf(user_msg); // BAD: Non-literal format string passed directly

description: Constant immutable string variable passed to printf().
rationale: Benign finding: AST analyzer flags non-literal identifier node, but the variable is an immutable compile-time string with no conversion specifiers.

description: Format string argument loaded from getenv() and passed to sprintf().
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: untrusted format string parameter in sprintf() allows stack inspection and buffer overflow.

description: sprintf() called with a hardcoded constant format string literal.
rationale: Benign finding: lexical regex rule flags any occurrence of sprintf() as CWE-134, but format string is completely static and safe.

description: User input read from stdin passed as format string to fprintf(stderr).
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: untrusted input directly passed as format string argument to fprintf().

description: Constant static diagnostic message variable passed to fprintf(stdout).
rationale: Benign finding: AST analyzer flags non-literal node type, but message string is fixed and immutable.
code_snippet: const char *prefix = "[INFO] Daemon active\n"; fprintf(stdout, prefix);

description: Untrusted event string from environment logged directly via syslog().
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: attacker can embed %s or %n in environment string to crash or exploit syslog daemon.

description: Constant static category tag variable passed to syslog().
rationale: Benign finding: AST analyzer flags identifier node, but string is an immutable static tag without conversion specifiers.

description: Table element containing untrusted environment string evaluated as format.
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: format string dynamically retrieved from array populated with untrusted data.

description: Static table of literal format strings indexed with constant subscript.
rationale: Benign finding: AST analyzer flags subscript expression tbl[0], but array elements are compile-time static literals.

description: Logging wrapper forwards parameter to printf() where caller supplies untrusted input.
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: wrapper receives untrusted parameter and passes it directly to format string argument of printf().

description: Internal logger receives only hardcoded literal string from callers.
rationale: Benign finding: AST analyzer flags parameter passed to printf(msg), but program context confirms only literal strings are ever passed.

description: Dynamic variable used as format specifier in snprintf().
rationale: Genuine vulnerability: user-controllable format string passed into snprintf().

description: snprintf() called with static format literal string.
rationale: Benign finding: lexical regex rule flags sprintf family call, but format template is a completely static string literal.
